title: Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP)
subtitle: Enucleate along the capsule, coagulate, then morcellate in a full bladder

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Management of Non-neurogenic Male LUTS
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: Bothersome lower urinary tract symptoms or retention from benign prostatic obstruction, any prostate size.
preparation: Prostate volume, flow, residual; PSA and cancer assessment where indicated.
Consent: retrograde ejaculation (most), temporary incontinence, bleeding, infection, stricture, bladder injury from the morcellator.
equipment: Holmium laser with a 550 micron end-firing fibre, continuous-flow laser resectoscope, morcellator with nephroscope, saline irrigation, three-way catheter, laser goggles.
anatomy: Verumontanum, external sphincter, bladder neck, ureteric orifices, the surgical capsule.
criticalSafety: Release the apex early and gently to protect the sphincter.
Morcellate only with a full bladder and the blades in view.
commonErrors: Pulling at the apex and tearing the sphincter.
complications: Urethral stricture or bladder neck contracture.
postop: Catheter for about one day; trial without catheter.

steps.emphasis: Note the ureteric orifices, the median lobe and the verumontanum before any laser.
Coagulate capsular vessels with the laser before morcellation; it is far harder after.
Inspect the capsule and the bladder wall after morcellation.
All morcellated tissue sent for histology.

step.holep.laser-safety.title: Laser safety check
step.holep.laser-safety.why: A holmium laser damages eyes and burns drapes. The laser officer, goggles, signs and fibre are checked before the first firing.
how: Confirm the laser safety officer, the warning sign on the door and goggles for everyone in the room.
Inspect the fibre tip and set the energy and frequency per protocol; standby until the fibre is in the scope.
Fire only with the fibre tip visible beyond the scope.
pitfalls: Firing with the fibre tip inside the scope.

step.holep.enucleation.title: Find the capsule plane and release the apex
step.holep.enucleation.why: The adenoma peels off the surgical capsule like an orange segment. An early, gentle apical release protects the external sphincter and continence.
how: Make incisions at the bladder neck (5 and 7 o'clock, or 6 o'clock) down to the capsule, from the bladder neck towards the verumontanum.
At the verumontanum, open the plane between adenoma and capsule and use the scope beak to sweep the adenoma off the capsule.
Release the apical mucosa early with the laser rather than tearing it with the scope.
pitfalls: Tearing the apical mucosa with traction.

step.holep.lobes.title: Enucleate the lobes into the bladder
step.holep.lobes.why: Following the capsule all the way round leaves a smooth, wide channel with little residual tissue.
how: Enucleate the median lobe (if present) and push it into the bladder.
Enucleate each lateral lobe from apex to bladder neck along the capsule (or en bloc in one piece).
Free each lobe at the bladder neck, keeping away from the ureteric orifices.
pitfalls: Undermining the trigone at the bladder neck.

step.holep.morcellation.title: Morcellation in a full bladder
step.holep.morcellation.why: The morcellator blades suck in anything they touch. A full bladder keeps the wall away; the blades must always be in view.
how: Exchange to the nephroscope and fill the bladder well, using two inflow sources if available.
Bring the morcellator to a floating adenoma piece, pedal suction first and cut only with the tissue held in the mouth of the blade.
Stop if vision is lost or the bladder empties.
pitfalls: Cutting without seeing the blade window.

step.holep.morcellator-injury.title: Bailout: bladder wall caught by the morcellator
step.holep.morcellator-injury.why: A morcellator injury can perforate the bladder. Stop at once, assess and repair rather than continuing.
how: Stop morcellating and release the pedal; inspect the bladder wall.
A superficial injury: coagulate and continue carefully, or leave fragments for a second session.
A full-thickness or intraperitoneal perforation: abandon, drain with a catheter and arrange repair; call a senior.
